Replace.Text: Military units from the city state of {1_CityStateName} have joined your army!
The units from the city state of {1_CityStateName} will now return home.

Provides 5 [ICON_GOLD] Gold per turn. Six of these must be built before the Domesday Book may be constructed in London. May only be built in a city 8 or more tiles from London that was originally controlled by Anglo-Saxon England.

The Domesday Shire Court, utilized during the reign of William the Conqueror for the purposes of tax assessment, was an assemblage of townspeople and local lords brought together for the Domesday survey. The Shire Court was loathed by the English populace, who begrudgingly reported their land and livestock holdings to the royal officers of the court.

Build Domesday Shire Courts to commission a survey of this shire of England. Once the building is complete you will gain tax revenue from the citizens of this region of England. When you have 6 of these courts completed, you are ready to build the Domesday Book in London and complete your conquest of England.
Win the scenario by building this in London. May not be built until you have 6 Domesday Shire Courts in your empire.

The Domesday Book, documenting the livestock and land holdings of the people of England during the rule of William the Conqueror, was recorded during the Domesday survey in 1085 AD. Conceived of by William as a means to assess the unpaid taxes under Edward the Confessor, the Domesday would come to be known as "the Book of Judgement," as all entries made by the royal officers in the book were final.
The completion of the Domesday Book wonder means that your great survey of England is complete and you have become master of these lands. Build it to win the scenario.

SCENARIO DESCRIPTION[NEWLINE]Hail to thee, great Viking lord! King Edward the Confessor of England is dead. The Saxon Harold Godwinson, Under-king to Edward, has quickly seized the throne. But his claim is a tenuous one: William of Normandy, Harald Hardrada of Norway, and King Sweyn of Denmark are in line for the throne as well. Can you don the mantle of one of these Viking Lords and become the next great King of England? Board your ships and prove to the world your right to be Odin's chosen warrior.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]VICTORY CONDITIONS[NEWLINE]You must complete the Domesday Book national wonder in London before time elapses to win the scenario. You must build 6 Domesday Shire Court buildings in cities originally controlled by Anglo-Saxon England before you can start the Domesday Book. These Shire Courts can only be constructed in cities 8 or more tiles from London.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]SPECIAL RULES[NEWLINE]All 4 major powers are locked at war with each other for the entire scenario. The Science, Policy, and Happiness systems are all off. You will not gain any new technologies or social policies during the game. All cities you control or conquer can grow unchecked without worrying about Happiness. If you gain a city-state ally, their military units are placed under your control for the duration of the alliance. All units possess the Defensive Embarkation promotion.

The kingdom of Denmark, having thrived throughout the 8-11th centuries AD during the height of the Viking age, would become embroiled in an ongoing war with Norway during the early 11th century. Harald Hardrada, King of Norway, who disputed Sweyn's right to the Danish throne after the passing of King Magnus I in 1047, would become the primary rival of the Danish King Sweyn II. For years the two would engage in military skirmishes, until finally reconciling after nearly 15 years when it became clear neither would be the victor.

With the death of Edward the Confessor in 1065, the English throne was quickly awarded to Harold Godwinson by the council of English noblemen known as the “Witenagemot”. Not long after, invasions by the Norwegian King Harald Hardrada and more importantly William, Duke of Normandy, would change the political landscape of England forever. Successfully defeating Harald at the Battle of Stamford Bridge in September of 1066, Godwinson would have to quickly regroup and head south to face William only a few short weeks later. However, the Norman armies led by William would prove too much for Godwinson. They would crush Harold's forces at the Battle of Hastings in 1066, leaving Harold dead and England open for the taking.

The Duchy of Normandy, formed in the region of France known as Rouen, was originally colonized by the Vikings of Scandinavia in the late 9th century AD. Formally created by the signing of the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte in 911, King Charles III of France would concede the territory to the Viking leader Rollo, creating the foundations of what came to be known as Normandy. William the Conqueror, the Duke of Normandy, would serve as its most famous leader, capturing the throne of England in 1066.

Norway, under the rule of King Harald “Hard Ruler” Sigurdsson, would embark on numerous military campaigns against Denmark in an attempt to usurp the Danish throne during the 11th century. After the death of Magnus I in 1047, Harald disputed the notion that Sweyn II was the legitimate ruler of Denmark and the two became notorious rivals. Despite several attempts, Harald was never successful in conquering Sweyn, and instead set his sights on the English throne. In September of 1066, Harald would invade England, only to be killed at the Battle of Stamford Bridge by the armies of Harold Godwinson.
King Edward the Confessor is dead. The throne of England is up for grabs. Can you lead your warriors to victory defeating the other Viking claimants to the throne?

Harold Godwinson was briefly the King of England, ruling from January 1066 until his defeat at the Battle of Hastings in October of that same year, and was the last of the Anglo-Saxon kings. Despite having successfully warded off the invasion of Harald Hardrada in the north, Godwinson and his army would be obliterated in a day-long battle less than a month later by William the Conqueror. Godwinson, legend has it, fell to an arrow through the eye.

Harald Sigurdsson, also known as Harald "Hardrada" or Harald the Hard Ruler, was King of Norway from 1047 until 1066. Hardrada is remembered most notably for his invasion of England and his subsequent defeat at the Battle of Stamford Bridge in September 1066, which unofficially marks the end of the Viking Age.

Sweyn II was King of Denmark from 1047 until 1074. During his rule, a longstanding feud with Harald Hardrada of Norway (who frequently attempted to conquer Sweyn) would lead to numerous battles between the two foes. During his lifetime Sweyn would father over 20 children, including 5 future kings of Denmark who would peacefully succeed one another for the next 60 years.

William the Conqueror (also known as William I) was the leader of the Norman Conquest of England, and would rule as England's first Norman king. Having defeated the army of Harold Godwinson at the Battle of Hastings in October of 1066, William would eventually quash the English resistance and rule for over 20 years until his death in 1087.
New recruits have heard tales of the plunder and land available in England. You can find {1_NumUnits} new units near your capital.
Tax collectors have returned from the shires of England. {1_GoldCollected} [ICON_GOLD] Gold was collected from the townsfolk.
Allows embassies to be established in other civilization's capitals
Doubles the defense strength of embarked units
Allows embarked units to cross oceans
Automate all [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Worker[ENDCOLOR] actions. The unit will continue working until you cancel its automation.
No reachable areas to explore at the moment.
This order tells the unit to explore the uncharted regions on the map. The unit will continue to move until it has run out of places to explore.
Allows establishing an additional trade route.
How can I get my advisors on the horn?

During play, your Advisors will appear in "pop-ups" when they have something they think you should know. They'll often provide links to other information that relates to the current topic. You can follow these links or click "Thank You" at any time to dismiss the Advisor.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]You can also press the "Additional Information" button in the upper right-hand corner of the screen to reach the "Advisor Counsel" screen. There you can see all four of your Advisors; if they have anything useful to say on the current situation it will appear there.
Why is the economic advisor so great?
The Economic Advisor provides advice on building and improving your cities and territory.
The foreign advisor is one pretty girl, but how can she help me?
The Foreign Advisor advises you on exploration and your relations with city-states, and other civilizations.

As leader of a mighty civilization, you have an able coterie of Advisors who will assist you with guidance and advice. They'll point out things that they believe are important, or that you might have forgotten about. You can turn them off if you like, but you may want to try playing with them for a while first. You have four different Advisors. Each provides advice on a specific area of expertise:
Why is the military advisor so totally awesome?
The Military Advisor provides advice on combat and all things related to war.
This science guy looks nerdy. Does Poindexer do anything cool?
The Science Advisor gives you advice on science and technology, as well as information on game rules.
How can I get the advisors to shut up?

You can determine how much assistance you get from the Advisors on the "Options" screen. You can set the advice level to New to Civ, New to Civ 5, Experienced Player, or No Advice. If turned off, they won't ever appear in pop-ups, but you can still go to the "Advisor Counsel" screen to see what they're thinking.

An interest in Archaeology has bloomed in your civilization! [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Antiquity Sites[/COLOR] have been revealed on the map, marking the locations of historically important events.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Building an Archaeologist will allow you to either [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]extract an Artifact[/COLOR] from the site, or [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]create a Landmark[/COLOR].

The Artists' Guild allows you to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]generate Great Artists[/COLOR] by assigning specialists to it. A Great Artist is a new type of Great Person that allows you to create [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Great Works of Art[/COLOR], essential for generating [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism and winning a Culture Victory.
You Can Build an Artists' Guild!

Cities can be tough to capture. Not only are their defenses strong, but they fight back, damaging or destroying your attacking units. Attack with multiple strong units on the same turn to capture enemy cities.

The enemy unit you are near is fortified. This means that it has a special defensive bonus (indicated by a shield flag). Fortified units are extremely difficult to defeat one-on-one, so consider attacking with multiple units in the same turn.
That battle didn't go our way. Perhaps with a little more planning we can reclaim our glory on the battlefield. Make sure to use the combat preview before attacking!
We may want to reconsider this attack; you will do marginal damage to your opponent and they will do considerable damage to you.
This Attack May Not End Well
Our treasury is depleted, and we need new sources of [ICON_GOLD]gold! Without [ICON_GOLD]gold, our research stagnates and we fall behind other civilizations.
Barbarian camps are vile places that are to be eradicated as soon as possible! Barbarian camps spawn more barbarians, and the sooner you destroy them the less trouble they'll be.
It is a dangerous world and we are vulnerable to attack. I suggest that you [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]build additional military units[/COLOR] to explore and to defend our civilization.
Our capital has grown into a bustling city! It may be time to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]build a Settler[/COLOR] to found another city.

You've discovered a valuable Artifact at your dig! You will need to choose to either [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]extract the Artifact[/COLOR] which you can use to generate [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism, or you can create a Landmark to generate [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.

The time has come to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]choose a new path[/COLOR] for your people and your empire! Each Ideology (Freedom, Order, and Autocracy) contains a unique set of increasingly powerful Tenets that will form the foundation of your Ideology, and influence your diplomatic relationships for years to come.

Your spy is reporting that they have gathered enough intelligence to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]steal a technology[/COLOR]. They are waiting for your decision on which technology you want them to steal.

Cities are formidable targets that often require 4 or more units to capture. When you attack them in melee, the cities will damage your attacking unit. They also have a ranged bombard attack that will be used against any besiegers. Are you sure you want to proceed in the attack?
Cities can bombard nearby enemies and damage or kill them. [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Order your city to bombard the enemy troops![/COLOR]
Our capital city has finished building a unit. Cities can build units, buildings, and wonders of the world, but only one at a time.

This is the city screen. It allows you to change what this city is building. On this screen you can also spend [ICON_GOLD]gold to purchase tiles around the city to expand your territory, and you can tell the city's citizens which tiles to work.
You have discovered a city-state! City-states are small countries that are not competing to win the game. You may interact with them diplomatically, or you may go to war with them.

A city-state has requested your assistance! If you provide help, you will gain Influence with the city-state. Once your Influence reaches a high enough level, the city-state will provide your civilization with various benefits.

While you can march military units in a city-state's territory, they certainly don't like it when you do. If you want to remain on good terms with a city-state, try to keep your military out of their borders.

We have built up enough [ICON_INFLUENCE] Influence with a city-state to become friends! To see what bonuses we receive from this, click on the city-state. Our [ICON_INFLUENCE] Influence will slowly decline over time, so continue to help the city-state or provide it with gifts of [ICON_GOLD] to maintain our friendship level.
Cities, like military units, defend against attackers. A city can only be captured when its strength is reduced to zero. Use military units to defeat the besiegers before our city falls!

One of your military units is near an enemy unit. To attack, order a combat unit to move into a tile occupied by the enemy. In combat, both the attacking and defending units may take damage, and one might be destroyed.
Having a strong Navy is the only way to defend and explore the oceans around our civilization. They can also wreak havoc among the enemy with their strong ranged attacks!

A new age of international cooperation has dawned with the founding of the World Congress! Your civilization, if either the host of the congress, or the civilization with the most [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]delegates[/COLOR], can [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]propose resolutions[/COLOR] that will have an effect on the entire world.

Because you're either the host, or have the most delegates, you're able to propose a Resolution. You can choose resolution that can help your people, or apply pressure to others. Some Resolutions have diplomatic consequences, so choose carefully!

This session of the World Congress is coming to a close, so it's time to use your Delegates to vote.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Keep in mind that you can also use your spies as [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Diplomats[/COLOR] to trade for votes, or to gain insight into how other leaders will vote.

The Culture Overview screen allows you to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]track and manage your Culture and Tourism[/COLOR]. You can move your Great Works from building to building, as well as track your level of Tourism versus other players, essential to a Culture Victory.
Natural Wonders are hidden around the world. Discovering them makes your civilization happier. If you build a city adjacent to them, you get a significant benefit. Explore the world to find more!
Please don't tell me this again.

Thanks to your research, all of your future military units will possess the "Embark" promotion and can move across the water. To embark a land unit, simply order it to move into a water tile. Embarked units are defenseless, so consider escorting them with military vessels.
All your units have orders and there is nothing else you can do this turn. Press the 'Next Turn' button to proceed to the next turn.
Our spy reports that the target civilization has no technology that we need. We should probably move our spy to a better target.
They have nothing that we need.
What if there is no more technology to steal?

After your spy has established surveillance in a target civilization, they will automatically start "Gathering Intelligence". If they discover that there are no technologies that you need, then you will receive a notification to let you know. You can then choose to move your spy to a better target, or instead leave your spy in the target civilization to watch for Intrigue. Intrigue is intercepted information that you can deliver to other civilizations. For example, you may have a spy in Arabia, and he may discover that they are planning to invade Egypt. You can then inform Egypt of this plot, and receive a diplomatic relationship boost as a result.

The Espionage Screen gives you a full overview of your Intelligence network. You can use it to check on the current status of your spies. But this is also [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]the command center from where you give orders to your spies[/COLOR]: be it to move to a different city, to establish surveillance or to steal a technology.
A spy has stolen technology from you! You should consider constructing defensive buildings like the Constabulary or Police Station, or using some of your own spies for counter-intelligence.
How do I use spies to steal technology?

Your spies can steal technology from a more advanced civilization. To attempt to steal technology, first, move a spy to a target city within another civilization. Once the spy arrives, there will be a period of time where they are "Establishing Surveillance" (noted in the "Activity" column). Once surveillance is established, you will know whether the target has technology that you can steal. If they do, the time it takes to steal the technology depends on how much science the target city is producing, and the rank of your spy. The higher your rank, the more quickly you will be able to steal technology. The higher the science output, the faster your spy can work.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Other factors that can affect the time it takes to steal technology includes defensive buildings like the Police Station or the Great Firewall wonder, which can stop a spy completely. Additionally, if the target has placed a defensive spy in the same city, your spy can be caught, or even killed (he will be taken out of action for multiple turns). This, of course, will have a negative effect on your diplomatic relations with the target civilization.

We have more than one of the same luxury resource improved. Our civilization receives [ICON_HAPPINESS_1]happiness for the first one but not for the others. We can trade the additional luxuries with other civilizations for their luxuries (or other resources) we don't have access to. Trade your excess luxuries with a friendly neighbor!

You've unlocked the ability to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]construct a Caravan[/COLOR], the earliest Trade unit available. Once built, you can establish a Trade Route with a city in another civilization that will generate [ICON_GOLD] Gold.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Although you start with the ability to create just a single Trade Route, additional Trade Route slots can be earned as your civilization becomes more advanced.
You Can Build a Trade Unit!

You have earned your first [ICON_PEACE] Faith point.[ICON_PEACE] Faith can be used to found a Pantheon, to spawn Great Prophets, and once you have founded a religion to buy Missionaries, Inquisitors and Religious Buildings. Mouse over the [ICON_PEACE] Faith icon in the top menu bar to see how much more [ICON_PEACE] Faith you need for the next threshold.

The unwavering Faith of your people has inspired a Great Prophet to emerge![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Since this is your first Great Prophet I strongly recommend you use him to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Found a Religion[/COLOR]. This way you have full control over the Beliefs that the Religion will give you. There are a limited amount of Religions allowed in each game, so claim yours as quickly as you can.

Spies can be used either offensively or defensively. To give your spy instructions, open the Espionage screen, which can be found under the Additional Information button on the upper right of the screen.

This is a good place to found a city. Food and resources are plentiful here. To found the city, press your Settler's [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Found City[/COLOR] button in the unit's action panel on the left side of the screen
Consider sending your Warrior out to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]explore new territory[/COLOR]. When a unit is selected, right-click on a tile to have that unit move there.
Clever move! We crushed our opponents without taking much damage ourselves!
This a clever move! This attack will do a lot of damage to your opponent without your units taking much damage.
Ancient Ruins hold secrets that may advance our civilization! [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Send a unit into an Ancient Ruin[/COLOR] to see what it holds.

The arts are thriving! If you're attempting a [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Culture Victory[/COLOR], you may want to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]create a Great Work of Art[/COLOR] to generate [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism for your civilization, essential for a Culture Victory. Or, you could start a Golden Age!
Thanks to your military victories, a Great General has come forth! Great Generals can stack with military units and provide a huge benefit to ones nearby!

Music has enchanted our people! If you're attempting a [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Culture Victory[/COLOR], you may want to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]create a Great Work of Music[/COLOR] to generate [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism for your civilization. Or, you could perform a Concert Tour in another civilization to provide a one-time boost to your [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism!

Congratulations, a great person has emerged from your civilization! These brilliant individuals can do a number of things for you: start a golden age, construct a unique tile improvement on the map, or use their special power to great effect!

Great Prophets can be used to found a Religion (if you have already founded a Pantheon), to enhance an existing Religion, to spread the religion to other cities or to build a tile improvement that generates [ICON_PEACE] Faith.

Creativity abounds in your civilization! If you're attempting a [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Culture Victory[/COLOR], you may want to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]create a Great Work of Writing[/COLOR] to generate [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism for your civilization. The more Tourism you generate, the better your chances of winning a Culture Victory!

Keeping your citizens happy is key to a productive civilization. Citizens produce [ICON_HAPPINESS_4] unhappiness, while luxury resources and some buildings provide [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] happiness to counteract it. Try to keep your civilization happy to keep it healthy!

Your people are no longer happy. An [ICON_HAPPINESS_4]unhappy populace will not grow as fast as a content one. If you wish to make your citizens happier, [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]order your Workers to build Improvements on resources[/COLOR].
Click on the diplomacy panel to learn more about our relationships with our neighbors. This provides us with all essential information regarding our diplomatic agreements and treaties.
If you wish to communicate with a civilization or city-state again, you may click on their city banner as a shortcut to talk with them.

Your Great Works are drawing visitors from every corner of the globe! To win a [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Culture Victory[/COLOR] you should continue increasing your [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism as much as possible. You can boost your [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism with bonuses from Open Borders, Trade Routes, Hotels, and more!
You need to found a city - and soon! Click your Settler's [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Found City[/COLOR] button as soon as possible.
You have a unit that hasn't moved for a while. Perhaps you should send it out to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]explore the world[/COLOR].

We have no military units defending our territory. It's useful to have one or more military units in our territory to fend off roving barbarians and to discourage other civilizations from attempting sneak attacks.
Our treasury has grown and we have money to spend. You can use money to purchase tiles to expand your territory, purchase influence over City-States, upgrade your units, or bribe other civilizations.
We have so many military units it is slowing our cities' [ICON_PRODUCTION]production. [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Stop building new military units[/COLOR] until our infrastructure can handle more.
Thanks for the information, but don't remind me again.
Forests slow down unit movement. Moving into a tile with a forest will often consume all of a unit's movement points. Forests block the view of objects behind them.

Hills slow down unit movement, but provide a sight advantage by allowing the unit to see over trees and other hills. Moving into a tile with a hill will often consume all of a unit's movement points. Hills block the view of objects behind them.

Jungles slow down unit movement. Moving into a tile with a jungle will often consume all of a unit's movement points. Jungles block the view of objects behind them. Jungles are often quite hot and humid, but that doesn't matter.
Marshes slow down unit movement. Moving into a tile with a marsh will often consume all of a unit's movement points. Units have a difficult time defending when they are in a marsh, so be careful!
Land units cannot move through mountains; you must move around them. Mountains can be seen from quite a distance away.

Moving across rivers slows down unit movement. Moving across a river will often consume all of a unit's movement points. It is extremely difficult for units to fight well when attacking across a river, so position your units carefully.

The Musicians' Guild allows you to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]generate Great Musicians[/COLOR] by assigning specialists to it. A Great Musician is a new type of Great Person that allows you to create [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Great Works of Music[/COLOR], essential for generating [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism and winning a Culture Victory.
You Can Build a Musicians' Guild!
That battle was a wash. We neither gained an advantage, or critically injured our opponent. You'll need to bring another unit in to support our troops.
This attack will damage both sides evenly. It's a good idea to continue this attack if you have multiple units nearby to wear them down before they can do the same to you!
Only one military unit can occupy a tile at a time. During its turn a military unit can pass through other military units, but may not end its turn in an occupied space.

You now have a ranged unit. Ranged units may attack enemies more than one tile away, but they are easily destroyed when attacked by melee units. Keep them safe behind your front line and they will serve you well.

The city we recently occupied is not yet excited about being part of our civilization and is causing a great amount of [ICON_HAPPINESS_4]unhappiness. If we construct a courthouse in that city, the citizens will not be as [ICON_HAPPINESS_4]unhappy.

Your people rejoice! You have accumulated enough [ICON_PEACE] Faith [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]to found a Pantheon[/COLOR], the first step towards founding a Religion.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]After clicking on the Notification below, you will see a selection of Pantheon Beliefs that are available to you. They are generally terrain-based, so choose something you think will help you based on your surroundings.

The sermons of your Great Prophet have been heard and you can now [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]found a Religion[/COLOR]. Choose a symbol along with its name. After that you will get to choose two additional Beliefs for your new Religion: A Founder Belief (player-level bonuses for the player that founds the Religion) and a Follower Belief (city-level Belief that applies to any city where your Religion spreads).

This overview contains three sections. The first is dedicated to your Religion. You can check your religious status, chosen Beliefs and even automate [ICON_PEACE] Faith purchases if you want to. The second section will give you an overview of the other World Religions and the third will show you which Beliefs are already taken and by whom.

The city we recently occupied is causing a great amount of [ICON_HAPPINESS_4]unhappiness. Building a Courthouse in that city will address their discontent, but we lack the research to do so. Research Mathematics so we can construct the Courthouse and they can be happy members of our civilization.
My studies show that your people trust your leadership. Keep exploring and meeting other civilizations, for who knows where the future may lead? We may reach the stars one day!

You can use the right mouse button to direct your units' movement. With a unit selected, right click on a tile and the unit will move to that tile. If you hold down the right mouse button, you'll see which tiles the unit can move to in a single turn.

The City List displays all the cities in your civilization. You can use this list to get a quick overview of what your civilization is currently doing and to easily change production if you go to war.
The Diplomacy List displays all the Civilizations and City-States that you've come in contact with and their score. Clicking on an entry will get you in contact with them.

The Diplomacy Overview is your gateway into all diplomatic information. You can see the diplomatic status between Civilizations, look at existing trade deals, and what resources are available for trade with other Civilizations.
The Economic Overview provides an in-depth look at all your cities. You can also investigate your [ICON_GOLD]gold income and what you're spending [ICON_GOLD]gold on.

The Diplomatic Trading screen allows civilizations to make diplomatic exchanges. Each side can build an offer from the list on their side, and then suggest it to the other side. Once both sides agree, the items in the trading screen are exchanged.
The Military Overview provides an in-depth look at all the units in your civilization, as well as how much supply your units are consuming and progress toward earning a Great General.

In the Production Chooser a unit, building, or wonder is selected to be produced in a city. A city can only work on a single item at a time. Every time your city completes a production, you'll be prompted again to have it build something new.

The Social Policy screen allows you to choose the Social Policies that will shape your civilization. You spend your accumulated [ICON_CULTURE]culture to unlock Social Policies. Some branches may not be selected until a technological era is reached. Also, some branches cannot be used together. (Look at the mouseover text to determine which ones are mutually exclusive.)
The Tech Chooser allows you to select a technology that your civilization will research. When a technology has been discovered, you'll be prompted to select a new one to research.
The Tech Tree provides a birds-eye view of the technologies that may be discovered and how they are connected. Connections show the requirements needed to unlock new technologies.
The Unit List shows all your units that you have under your command. You may select them to find where they are on the map and give them orders.

You can found a new city with your Settler. In order to grow, a city requires a number of quality [ICON_FOOD] food tiles nearby, so found your city next to [ICON_FOOD] food resources. [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Move your Settler to a fertile location and found a new city.[/COLOR]

Your Settler is alone outside your borders and could be captured. [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Order a military unit to escort your Settler[/COLOR] to protect them from barbarians and opportunistic enemy civilizations.
Siege units are excellent at knocking out cities from range, but are defenseless if attacked by other units, so always defend them!

Using the Espionage screen (found in the Additional Information button on the upper right of the screen) you can set your spies up either offensively (to spy and steal in foreign territory) or defensively (to protect your cities and technologies).

Other civilizations are starting to notice the grandeur of your Culture! In terms of a Culture Victory, [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]consider [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism your "Offense"[/COLOR] against other civilizations, [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]and Culture your "Defense"[/COLOR] from other civilizations.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Click on the [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism icon at the top of the screen to track how you're faring against the Culture of other civilizations.
I am your science advisor. In this lesson I'll teach you how to move your units around the map. In the process you'll discover ancient ruins, Natural Wonders, and whole new continents!
I am your economic advisor. In this lesson I'll teach you how cities work, how to found new cities, and where the best places are to build them.

I am your economic advisor. In this lesson I'll teach you how to use Workers to enhance your cities. Under your command your Workers will build city connections to collect [ICON_GOLD]gold, construct improvements to help your cities grow faster and build things quicker, and improve resources to make our people happier.
I'm your military advisor and you can guess why I'm here. In this lesson I'll teach you how to stomp out barbarians and destroy their camps, and how to conquer an enemy civilization's city.

I'm your foreign advisor. In this lesson you'll learn the basics of diplomacy with other civilizations and city-states. This is a complicated subject, so for now we will concentrate upon two important concepts: developing influence over a city state and trading resources with a neighboring civilization.

Settlers require 2 [ICON_CITIZEN] population to build, so to speed you on your way we gave your first city an extra [ICON_CITIZEN] population. Don't get used to it; cities founded from here on out will start with only 1 [ICON_CITIZEN] population.

We have a unit that is on the verge of being destroyed. Wounded units are much less effective in combat and are easily killed, so consider moving it to a safe location and ordering it to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Fortify Until Healed[/COLOR].

You can upgrade obsolete units, turning them into more powerful units by spending [ICON_GOLD]gold. To upgrade a unit, move it into your territory and the upgrade unit button will appear. [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Press the upgrade button[/COLOR] to improve your obsolete unit.

Your people are very [ICON_HAPPINESS_4]unhappy. Our cities have drastically reduced [ICON_PRODUCTION]production and our units will not fight as well. Make your people happier by building happiness buildings, constructing improvements on resources, and trading for resources with other leaders.
There is more than one way to become the greatest civilization and win the game. In fact here are four routes: through military, technology, diplomacy, or culture!

Now that we have a Worker, we can order them to construct Improvements to boost the productivity of our territory. [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Move your Worker to a highlighted tile and construct an improvement.[/COLOR]

We have a Worker, but have not improved any tiles yet. [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Order your Worker to construct an improvement[/COLOR] on a tile near one of your cities to gain an economic benefit.

Workers are defenseless, so use extreme caution when moving them outside our borders. Since we only have one city at the moment, we should [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]keep our Workers within our territory[/COLOR].
I think we have enough Workers for the moment. You may want to build something else in your city.
The land near your city could be made more productive. [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Build a Worker[/COLOR] to improve your territory.
Work boats allow you to improve fish and whale resources off your coast. Once you improve those locations, the work boats will be permanently converted.

The Writers' Guild allows you to [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]generate Great Writers[/COLOR] by assigning specialists to it. A Great Writer is a new type of Great Person that allows you to create [COLOR_ADVISOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Great Works of Writing[/COLOR], essential for generating [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism and winning a Culture Victory.
You Can Build a Writers' Guild!

{1_CityName:textkey} is landlocked, which means it doesn't have access to the water. So you have to worry more about bears than sharks.

{1_CityName:textkey} would benefit greatly from having the surrounding tiles improved. Consider getting a Worker to help it out.

Air units do not move around the map like ground and naval units. They must be "based" on a player-owned friendly city. Fighters and some bombers can be based upon aircraft carriers as well. Missile units may be based on cities, nuclear submarines, and missile cruisers. Air units cannot embark. If on extended sea voyages, they must be carried by the appropriate vessel - carrier, cruiser, or nuclear sub.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Anti-air units and helicopters don't need to be based. They move around the map like other units, and can embark.
How does range for air units work?

In place of a movement stat, air units have "range." This is the distance from a base that they can perform "missions." It's also the distance that they can "rebase" - move from one base to another. For example, a fighter unit has a range of 8. It can perform its missions against any tile within 8 spaces of its current base, and it can move to another player owned base (city or carrier) that is within 8 spaces as well.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]An air unit that rebases cannot perform another mission in the same turn.

When a unit is ordered to make an "air strike" against an enemy city or unit, if it is not intercepted, it performs a ranged attack against the target. Unlike most ranged attacks, however, the attacking unit can take damage from the attack. (In another words, if you bomb a tank, it might hurt you.) If the air striking unit survives, it returns to its base.[NEWLINE]Missiles and bombers have the most powerful air strikes.
What are the rules for air strikes?
The air unit attacks a ground target within its air range.

When attacking a target that is heavily protected by fighters and AA units, a fighter can perform the "air sweep" mission against that target to "use up" the enemy's interception capability. If the fighter is intercepted by an enemy fighter, the two units dogfight, and one or the other might be damaged or destroyed. If the fighter is intercepted by a ground unit, it will take damage from the ground unit (but less so than a unit on an air strike mission would).
What are the rules for air sweeps?
The air unit "sweeps" a target tile, disabling "intercepting" units.

There are four main types of air units in Civilization V: helicopter gunships, missiles, fighters, and bombers. Helicopter gunships are the closest to standard ground combat units and will be discussed separately.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Of the other air units, missiles are essentially "one-shot" weapons: you fire 'em, they hit their target and they're gone. Fighters are primarily used to defend against other air power and to clear the target of interceptors to allow bombers to hit their targets. Bombers do damage to targets on the ground, if not intercepted. Anti-air units defend against fighters and bombers.
Missiles can be based on player-owned cities, on missile cruisers and on nuclear submarines.
Just how good are gunship helicopters against tanks?
Gunships can do serious damage to tank units (which is why most modern armor is accompanied by hefty anti-air assets on the modern battlefield).

The first nuclear weapon available in the game, the atomic bomb is a very powerful unit that can quickly alter the world's balance of power. Atomic bombs are similar to missiles in that they may only attack once. Unlike missiles, they may be stationed on aircraft carriers. The damage radius for the atomic bomb is 2 tiles in every direction. Units caught in the blast will be damaged, and cities will lose population if hit.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]An "A-bomb" cannot totally destroy a city. No matter how many times a city is hit by atomic bombs, it will not be destroyed.
What are the rules for atomic bombs?
Where can atomic bombers be based?
Atomic bombers can be based on cities and on aircraft carriers.
How do I know where a certain air unit can be based?
Different types of crafts may be based in different locations.
Bombers can be based on cities and aircraft carriers.
What air units can a carrier base?
Initially a carrier can carry two air units (fighters, bombers and atomic bombers). This capacity may be boosted through promotions.
What air units can a missile cruiser base?
A missile cruiser can carry up to three missiles of any type.
Where can fighters and jet fighters be based?
Fighters and jet fighters can be based on cities and aircraft carriers.

By the Second World War, air power has come to dominate warfare around the world. Air power acts as a "force multiplier" in combat, and the nation that can establish air supremacy over the battlefield has a huge advantage over the enemy.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Perhaps most importantly, strategic bombing has become a central force in modern warfare, and with the advent of nuclear ballistic missiles, it has the ability to literally wipe an entire civilization off the face of the planet.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Air power is critical to victory in Civilization V.
As stated above, helicopter gunships are quite similar to standard land units. They are extremely effective at killing tanks, but remain vulnerable to anti-aircraft fire.
How does interception work with air units?

Fighters and jet fighters can be set to "intercept" enemy air attacks. (AA gun, mobile SAM, and certain naval units automatically intercept; they don't need to be given a special mission.) If an air unit tries an air strike against a target within the range of an intercepting unit, the interceptor will fire on the attacker and do damage to it. Unless the attacker is killed by the interceptor, the air strike proceeds.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Only one unit can intercept an air strike, and once it does so, it cannot intercept any more that turn (though certain promotions can increase this). So if you're expecting multiple air attacks on a target, you might want to pile multiple fighters and AA units on and around that target.
The air unit prepares to defend against enemy air attacks. (Note that ground-based anti-air units automatically intercept when attacked by air; they don't need special orders.)
What are the rules for interception?
Missiles are one-shot weapons. They perform a single air strike mission against a target, and then, win or lose, they are destroyed. Unlike normal aircraft, missiles cannot be intercepted.
What are the rules for missiles?

During an air unit's turn, it can perform one of a number of "missions." These include making air strikes (ranged attacks against ground targets), rebasing, interception (defending against enemy air attack) and "sweeping" (disabling enemy interception). Some air units can perform only some of these missions.
What are the rules on gunship helicopter movement?
Gunships can move over all terrain types including mountains and ice, at a cost of 1 MP each. They can also move over coastal waters and deep water if they embark.
Which naval units can be bases for air units?
Some naval units can be used as bases for air units and these naval units may hold more than one air unit.

While the atomic bomb does a fair amount of damage, nuclear missiles are truly devastating. All units caught in the blast radius are destroyed, and the damage done to cities is even greater. Unlike atomic bombs, nuclear missiles are even capable of wiping cities off the map completely (note that a player's original capital may not be destroyed in this manner).[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]As their name implies, nuclear missiles are missile units, which means they may be stationed on missile cruisers or nuclear submarines, but not aircraft carriers.
What are the rules for nuclear missiles?
What air units can a nuclear submarine base?
A nuclear submarine can carry up to two missiles of any type.
How can an air unit change bases?
The air unit moves to a new base within its range. Up to 6 air units can base in a single city. This limit is raised to 10 if the city has an Airport.
What does the recon ability for air units do?

Fighters, jet fighters and stealth bombers have a special "recon" ability. At the start of their turn, everything within 6 tiles of their base is visible. This isn't a mission and it doesn't use up their turn: it happens automatically.
What are the stacking rules with air units?

You can have up to 6 missiles, fighters and bombers in a single city. This limit is raised to 10 if the city has an Airport. These units can be freely stacked with both combat and non-combat units.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Helicopters and anti-air units must follow the standard stacking rules.
Where can stealth bombers be based?
Stealth bombers can be based on cities only.

Your new item may not be traded again this turn.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]If you select a Great Work of Art for a slot but do not perform a swap on your turn, other civilizations may swap for it on their turn without your permission! Make sure you only display items that you are willing to part with!
Do not trifle with me. Continue settling cities near the mighty Songhai Empire and soon they will join us. This sword is not for show.
If your armies near my border have come to fight, I shall slay them. We are favored by God and cannot lose.
Your wanton aggression against {@1_MinorCivName} does not go unnoticed. You will face serious consequences should you continue assault.
If you're trying to get me upset, you're doing a good job. And if you keep expanding near Rome, you'll see me angry. Which you will very much regret.
Your soldiers near my empire seem to be quite excited lately. It couldn't be that their foolish leader wishes to pick a fight, could it?

Isabella's Spain and Pachacuti's Incan Empire
You must have at least 2 teams.
What are barbarians and ancient ruins?
What are ancient ruins and what do they do?

Ancient Ruins are the remnants of even earlier civilizations which rose and fell long before you came on the scene. Ruins provide a random benefit to the civilization of the unit that first enters their tile. The ruin is destroyed when it is entered.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Ruins are cool. Find as many as you can before other civs get to them!

Barbarians are roving bands of villains who hate civilization and everything that goes with it. They attack your units and cities and pillage your improvements. They're just not very nice at all.[NEWLINE]As your civilization grows the barbarians become much less menacing, but early in the game they can be a huge problem.
What happens if a barbarian captures a civilian unit?

If a barbarian unit comes upon a non-combat unit - settler or worker - the barbarians capture that unit. They will take it off to their nearest encampment, and the unit may be recovered by any player in the game. Should one of your civilians be captured in this manner, be sure to pursue and retrieve them before somebody else does! Great people are the exception. Barbarians will destroy a great person if they are found undefended.
How can an ancient ruin provide you with culture?
The ruin provides culture to your civilization.
What do you get if you destroy a barbarian encampment?
A civilization will earn a gold reward for dispersing a barbarian encampment - in addition to the benefit of stopping it from spawning more barbarian units, which of course is the primary reward.

Barbarians come from "encampments", which may appear randomly in any tile that cannot be seen by a unit. Every few turns the encampment will create another barbarian unit which will make a beeline for the nearest civilization and start causing trouble. The only way to stop this is to find the encampment and destroy it. Encampments are usually guarded by at least one unit, so they're not pushovers.
How can an ancient ruin help you with technology?
The ruin provides your civilization with a free technology.

During the early portion of the game - say, the first 25 - 50 turns - much of your energy should be involved in exploring the world. During your exploration you will be encountering ancient ruins and barbarians. Ancient ruins are good, barbarians are not.
How can an ancient ruin help you explore the map?
The ruin provides a map of the surrounding area (lifting the fog of war from a number of tiles).
What are these barbarians doing with boats!?

Barbarian encampments on the coastline can create naval units (again, equal to those that can be created by the civilization with the most advanced tech). These units will menace your coastline, destroy naval improvements and attack hapless land units which stray too near the coastline. It's important to maintain a navy to keep them off your back, but the best way to stop these attacks is to destroy the coastal encampments nearby.
How do new barbarian encampments show up?

Barbarian encampments may spring up in any neutral space which cannot be seen by a civilization's city or unit. If you want to keep barbarian encampments from popping up around your civilization, place units on hills to keep as much terrain in sight as possible.
How are unit experience points gained when battling barbarians?

When they fight barbarian units, your less well-trained units will gain experience points. However, any unit that has already acquired 30 XPs (or has exchanged that many for promotions) no longer gains XPs from fighting barbarians.
What benefits can you get from an ancient ruin?
Ancient ruins can provide a number of different benefits.
How can your cities gain population from an ancient ruin?
The ruin contains survivors from the earlier civilization. They move to one of your cities, increasing its population by one.
When will the barbarians be gone?

Barbarians can remain in the game right up until the end. However, as more land is acquired there will be less available for the barbarian encampments to spawn in. If the entire world is civilized, the barbarians will be gone.
How can an ancient ruin provide you with gold?
The ruin provides gold to your civilization!
What kind of units can barbarians use?

Barbarian encampments can create almost any kind of unit in the game - from warriors and spearmen to cannon and tanks. (They can build units equal to those that the most advanced civilization can create.)[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Once created the barbarian units will either hang around their encampment or head off toward the nearest civilization or city-state and try to cause trouble. They'll attack units, destroy improvements and menace cities. If enough are involved, they can take down a poorly-defended city, which is then thoroughly pillaged. A pillaged city may lose gold, buildings and population.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]This is why it's important to periodically sweep the countryside around your civilization, destroying encampments before they become a threat.
How can an ancient ruin upgrade one of your units?
The unit which enters the tile is upgraded to a more advanced unit (a warrior might become a swordsman, for example).
Can you get settler and worker from ancient ruins?
On easier difficulty levels, you can also receive free Settlers and Workers from ruins.
