To maximize your bonus, make sure the Great Work Slots are all filled with Music from the same Era and Civilization.
What happens to the buildings in captured cities?

If a city is captured, its World Wonders and Culture Buildings that hold Great Works are captured as well. A city's National Wonders are destroyed when the city is captured.[NEWLINE]The city's military buildings (Monument, Barracks, Walls, etc.) are always destroyed when the city is taken. All other buildings have a 66% chance of being captured intact.

A city is more than a bunch of homes. It contains schools and libraries, markets and granaries, banks and barracks. Buildings represent the improvements and upgrades that you make in a city. Buildings can increase the city's rate of growth, can speed production, can increase the science of a city, can improve its defenses, and can do lots of other good things as well. See the Civilopedia Building section for more details on buildings.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A city that has no buildings is pretty weak and primitive and will probably remain fairly small, while a city with a lot of buildings can indeed grow to dominate the world.

When a city is ready to construct something, the city's "Production Menu" will appear. If a building is available to be constructed, it will appear on this menu. Click on the building (or unit or Wonder) to order the city to begin construction.

"Krepost" is the Russian word for "fortress." For much of its history Russia was an expansionist state, pushing its borders further east across the vast steppes, into Siberia and beyond. When entering new terrain, the Russians often would construct a "krepost" to protect their troops and to house governmental and religious buildings. Depending upon the local situation and availability of materials, a krepost could be a temporary wooden fort or a more permanent and imposing stone defensive work. In many ways the krepost is similar in form and function to the ubiquitous forts that the Romans built in their newly-conquered lands.

The Krepost is the Russian unique building, replacing the barracks. The Krepost provides 15 experience points for all military units constructed in its city. In addition, the Krepost increases the city's cultural border growth by 25%. It's quite worthwhile to construct these useful buildings in all Russian cities, but especially in cities on the civilization's frontiers.

There's one downside to buildings: most of them cost gold to maintain. The price depends upon the building in question, and can range from 1 to 5 per turn. The gold is deducted from your treasury each turn. Buildings that incur maintenance can be sold via the City Screen if necessary. See the section on Gold for more details on maintenance.
What is the palace and what does it do for a city?

The palace is a special building. Part building, part Wonder, the palace automatically appears in the first city you build, which makes that city the capital of your empire. If your capital city is captured, your palace will automatically be rebuilt in another city, making that city your new capital. If you subsequently retake your original capital, the palace will move back to its original location.[NEWLINE]The palace provides a small amount of production, science, gold, and culture to your civilization. If you connect other cities to the capital by road or harbor, you will create city connections which generate additional income.

With the single exception of the monument, which has no prerequisites and is available to build at the start of the game, you need knowledge of a specific technology to construct a building. For example, you must learn bronze working before you can build a barracks.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Some buildings have resource prerequisites as well - for instance a city must have an improved source of horses or ivory nearby to construct a circus.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Also, some buildings have building prerequisites. You can't build a temple in a city unless you've already constructed a shrine there.
You can change a city's construction orders on the City Screen. You can also expend gold to purchase a building (or other item) on this screen as well. See the City Screen section for details.
How do buildings interact with specialists?

Certain buildings allow you to create "specialists" out of your citizens to work those buildings. Specialists improve the output of the building, and they also increase the city's output of Great People. See the section on Specialists and Great People for details.
Can only be built by Rotheram.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]+15 XP for air Units.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]+10% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production when building air units.

The Aerodrome can only be built by Rotheram. It replaces the Airship Hangar, providing a bonus to [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production when building air units: Flyers, Airships, and Sky Fortresses. Like the Airship Hangar, it also provides extra Experience to trained air units. Use the Aerodrome to build an experienced air fleet in a short time.
Provides [ICON_RES_ALUMINUM] Aetherium resources without needing to own a tile with the resource. With these resources, you can train more airship units for your army.

Can only be built by Cutler.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Provides [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]2 [ICON_RES_ALUMINUM] Aetherium[ENDCOLOR] resources.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Each source of [ICON_RES_ALUMINUM] Aetherium worked by this city provides +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold.

The Aetherium Factory can only be built by Cutler. Unlike the Aetherium Fabricator, which it replaces, the Aetherium Factory gives a bonus to [ICON_GOLD] Gold which increases with the number of [ICON_RES_ALUMINUM] Aetherium resources worked by the city it is built in. This bonus stacks with Cutler's trait.

Allows airlifts to or from this city. [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Increases air unit capacity of the city from 6 to 10.[ENDCOLOR] 50% of the [ICON_CULTURE] Culture from World Wonders, Natural Wonders, and Improvements (Landmarks, Moai, Chateau) is added to the [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism output of the city. [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism output from Great Works +50%.

The versatile Airport is an excellent choice for both civilizations that are trying to improve their [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism output or and those that need to use airlift capabilites to shuttle units to distant cities.
Provides extra Experience to trained air units: Flyers, Airships, and Sky Fortresses.

The Amphitheater increases the [ICON_CULTURE] Culture of a city, speeding the growth of the city's territory and the civilization's acquisition of Social Policies. The city must contain a Monument (or a Stele) before the Amphitheater can be constructed. Contains 1 slot for a Great Work of Writing.
Must have built a Difference Engine in all cities.
The Analytical Engine may only be built once each of your cities has a Difference Engine, and you may only build one in your empire. It provides a large boost to [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production.

Angkor Wat provides a free temple in every city, as well as a point of culture and a Great Engineer point. Since temples each provide +2 culture points, this wonder obviously provides a huge culture boost to a civilization.
40% of [ICON_FOOD] Food is carried over after a new [ICON_CITIZEN] Citizen is born.
The Aqueduct decreases the amount of [ICON_FOOD] Food a city needs to increase in size by 40%. Build Aqueducts in cities that you want to grow large over time.
+15 XP for all Units.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have a Barracks or Krepost.
The Armory provides experience for military units constructed in the city. The city must contain a Barracks before an Armory can be constructed.
City must have a Castle or Mughal Fort.

The Arsenal is a mid-game military building that increases a city's Defense Strength by 9 and Hit Points by 25, making the city more difficult to capture. The city must possess a Castle before it can construct an Arsenal.

Provides 2 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great Person Points (GPP) towards a Great Artist. Add up to two specialists to this building to gain [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and increase the rate of Great Artist acquisition (3 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and 3 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] GPP per specialist).

The Artists' Guild is the only building that contains artist specialist slots, which are critical for generating Great Artists. If your goal is a cultural victory, this building is a must-have. The Artists' Guild provides 2 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great Person Points, and each assigned specialist provides 3 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great Person Points and 3 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.
Unlocks Perpetual Motion Engine when built in every city.
Provides a large boost to [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production as well as some [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness. Build one in each city to unlock the Perpetual Motion Engine national wonder.

The Bank is a Renaissance-era building which increases the city's output of [ICON_GOLD] Gold. A city must possess a Market or Bazaar before a Bank may be constructed. Trade routes other players make to a city with a Bank will generate an extra 1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the city owner and the trade route owner gains an additional 1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the trade route.
Barracks provide experience for military units constructed in the city. This experience can be used to give the units Promotions, making them more effective in battle.

Provides 1 extra copy of each improved luxury resource near this City. Each source of [ICON_RES_OIL] Oil and each Oasis provides +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold. Trade routes other players make to a city with a Bazaar will generate an extra 1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the city owner and the trade route owner gains an additional 1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the trade route.

The Bazaar is the Arabian unique building, replacing the Market. The Bazaar provides a [ICON_GOLD] Gold bonus to the city. The civilization gains one additional copy of each luxury resource provided by a city possessing a Bazaar. The Bazaar provides +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold on [ICON_RES_OIL] Oil and Oases.

This expensive Wonder reduces the cost of purchasing buildings, units and Wonders in ALL cities by 25%. In addition, all specialists in all cities now provide +2 culture each. Finally, Big Ben provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 Merchant points.
Must have built a Grand Mansion in all cities.
The Biltmore House may only be built once each of your cities has a Grand Mansion, and you may only build one in your empire. It provides a boost to [ICON_GOLD] Gold and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.

[ICON_CULTURE] Culture and [ICON_GOLD] Gold costs of acquiring new tiles reduced by 25% in this city.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Must have built a Temple in all Cities and be an American Civilization. The cost goes up the more cities there are in the empire.

An important building for an American civilization trying to spread their religion world-wide from an empire with few, populous cities. It also increases border growth in this city. A civilization must have a Temple in all cities before it can construct the Blythe Intaglios.
Reduces population loss from nuclear attack by 75%.
Bomb Shelters reduce population loss from a nuclear attack on this city by 75%. Duck and Cover!
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"When you realize how perfect everything is, you will tilt your head back and laugh at the sky."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Gautama Buddha[NEWLINE][TAB]
The military/technology-oriented Brandenburg Gate provides a free Great General upon completion. In addition, the Wonder grants +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 Great Scientist points.
+33% [ICON_CULTURE] Culture in this City.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have a Museum.
A Broadcast Tower is a late-game building which increases [ICON_CULTURE] Culture output of the city by 33%. The city must possess a Museum before it can construct a Broadcast Tower.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Broadway is a main artery of New York cultural life - the hardened artery."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Walter Winchell[NEWLINE][TAB]
Requires no [ICON_GOLD] Gold maintenance.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Should this city be captured, the amount of [ICON_GOLD] Gold plundered by the enemy is doubled.

The Egyptians raised ancestor-worship to heights unmatched before or since, and much of their civilization's wealth and creative energy was expended in the construction of Burial Tombs for deceased relatives. Many such tombs may be found in the Valley of the Kings, across the Nile River from Thebes. These tombs were often stocked with a portion of the wealth of the deceased, making them rich targets for tomb robbers throughout history.

The Burial Tomb is a Classical-era building which increases the city's output of [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness, and costs no maintenance for the city. However, if the city is captured, the capturing civilization will gain twice as much gold as would be the case in a city without a Burial Tomb. It replaces the Temple.

Unique Indonesian Garden replacement. +25% [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great People generation in this City, and +2 [ICON_PEACE] Faith for each World Religion that has at least 1 follower in the city.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Unlike the Garden the Candi does not have to be built next to a River or Lake.

In addition to the regular abilities of the Garden, the Candi also provides +2 [ICON_PEACE] Faith for each World Religion that has at least 1 follower in the city. Only Indonesia may build it, and the city does not need to be located next to a River or Lake.
Land trade routes originating from this city have a 50% increase in range and produce an additional 2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold when connecting to another civilization.
The Caravansary is a Classical-era building. It improves the range and [ICON_GOLD] Gold yield of land trade routes.
Must have built a Philanthroporium in all cities.

The Carnegie Hall may only be built once each of your cities has a Philanthroporium, and you may only build one in your empire. It provides a large boost to [ICON_CULTURE] Culture as well as a small boost to [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness.
The Castle is a Medieval-era building which increases the city's Defensive Strength by 7 and Hit Points by 25. The city must possess Walls before the Castle can be constructed.
Can only be built in cities following a religion with the Cathedrals belief. Construct this building by purchasing it with [ICON_PEACE] Faith.
The Ceilidh Hall is a Renaissance-era building unique to the Celts, replacing the Opera House. It increases the city's [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness.

The Chateau is a Medieval-era building which increases the city's Defensive Strength. The city must possess Walls before the Chateau can be constructed. A Chateau is more expensive than the Castle, which it replaces, however it also provides [ICON_CULTURE] Culture to the city.

Chichen Itza increases a civilization's worker's construction speed by 50%. It also provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture point and +1 Great Engineer point. It's useful for any civilization that's concentrating upon improving the output of its cities.

Each plantation worked by this City produces +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold, except Cocoa Plantations which when worked by this city instead provide +3 [ICON_GOLD]. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have at least one plantation nearby.

The Chocolate House can only be constructed in a city with a plantation nearby. The Chocolate House increases the [ICON_GOLD] Gold output for each plantation by one and each improved Cocoa resource increases the [ICON_GOLD] Gold output by an additional 2.
City must have an improved source of [ICON_RES_HORSE] Horses or [ICON_RES_IVORY] Ivory nearby.
Must have built a Colosseum in all Cities. The cost goes up the more cities there are in the empire.

A massive stadium located in the heart of Rome, the Circus Maximus was the first, and largest, chariot racing venue in ancient Rome. At the time of its usage, it could hold over a quarter of a million people, over 25% of the city's population. Measuring over 2000 ft in length, twelve full-sized chariots could easily race side by side. Originally used by the Etruscan kings to host their entertainments and festivals, the first Roman Games were held at the racetrack by the fifth Roman King, Tarquinius Priscus. The site was later expanded by Julius Caesar in 50 BC to its current size.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The last recorded race was held in 549 AD by the Ostrogoth king Totila, and was later abandoned. Now the Circus is a public park, the track covered over in grass. Some of the original structures still remain, namely a few starting gates and medians, but now the Circus is mostly used to host live concerts and meetings on the open green.

This National Wonder increases [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness in the empire by 5. It also provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. A civilization must have a Colosseum in all cities before it can construct a Circus Maximus.
The Circus can only be constructed in a city with an improved source of [ICON_RES_HORSE] Horses or [ICON_RES_IVORY] Ivory nearby. The Circus increases a civilization's [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness.
+25% [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great People generation in this City.

The Coffee House is a Renaissance-era building unique to Austria, replacing the Windmill. It increases the city's [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and speed at which [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great People are generated by 25%.
The Colosseum increases a civilization's [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness. It cannot provide more Happiness than there are [ICON_CITIZEN] Citizens in a city.

The Colossus provides +1 gold from water tiles worked by this city (so it must be constructed on a coastal city). It also provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 Great Merchant points. Once you've constructed the Colossus, be sure to order its city's citizens to work as many water tiles as they can. This can provide a large early-game financial boost to your civilization.
Reduces enemy spy stealing rate by 25%.
Constabularies slow down the rate at which enemy spies can steal technologies from your city.
Eliminates extra [ICON_HAPPINESS_4] Unhappiness from an [ICON_OCCUPIED] Occupied City.

A Courthouse is a building in which the local authorities administer the law. Oftentimes the building also houses the local civil government as well, but this is by no means always the case. Generally the courthouse occupies a conspicuous place of importance in the central part of the city - either because the citizens view it with pride, or because the government wants to remind the citizens that it's got its eye on them.
The Courthouse reduces the unhappiness caused by captured cities. Construct one in each occupied city as quickly as possible, especially if you're intent upon conquering a bunch of them.
Upon completion of the Cristo Redentor wonder, the civilization immediately enters a Golden Age. In addition, this Wonder also provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 Great Artist points.
Unlocks the Analytical Engine when built in every city.
Provides a boost to [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and [ICON_RESEARCH] Science. Build one in each city to unlock the Analytical Engine national wonder.

Unique Polish Stable replacement. +15% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +15 XP for Mounted Units.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Each Pasture worked by this City produces +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
In addition to the regular abilities of the Stable, the Ducal Stable increases [ICON_GOLD] Gold on Pasture tiles and +15 XP for Mounted Units. Only the Polish may build it.

The East India Company increases the amount of [ICON_GOLD] Gold a city generates. Trade routes other players make to a city with an East India Company will generate an extra 4 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the city owner and the trade route owner gains an additional 2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the trade route.
The Eiffel Tower provides a large amount of happiness, as well as +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 Great Merchant points. This wonder is very helpful in getting Golden Ages in the Modern era.

The Factory is an Industrial-era building which greatly increases a city's [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production. The city must already possess a Workshop (or Longhouse). 1 [ICON_RES_COAL] Coal is consumed when a Factory is created.
+15% [ICON_FOOD] Food. Each worked Lake tile provides +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must be built next to a River or Lake.

A floating garden is a small artificial island constructed on a freshwater lake in order to increase the land available for agriculture. The lake irrigates the island and provides it with fresh organic material, resulting in an incredibly fertile growing environment. The Aztecs were masters of this form of agriculture, and the "Floating Gardens of Xochimilco" remain famous today.
The Floating Gardens is the Aztec unique building, replacing the Water Mill. It increases the city's [ICON_FOOD] Food output, and should be built if the city is near a lake or river.

The Forbidden Palace immediately increases your friendship level with all city states by 50% and it provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 Great Artist point. Obviously, this isn't especially useful if you plan to ignore or conquer your fellow city-states. But if you plan a diplomatic victory, this can greatly enhance your chances.

+15% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production when building Land Units.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Each source of [ICON_RES_IRON] Iron worked by this City produces +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have a mined source of Iron nearby.
The Forge can only be constructed in a city with an improved source of [ICON_RES_IRON] Iron nearby. It increases the speed at which the city produces land units.
The Ceilidh Hall is a Classical-era building unique to the Celts. It increases the city's [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness.

The Satrap's Court is the Persian unique building. The Satrap's Court increases the city's output of wealth. However, the Satrap's Court also increases the civilization's [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness. The city must have a Market before the Satrap's Court may be constructed.
+25% [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great People generation in this City.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must be built next to a River or Lake.
The Garden increases the speed at which [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great People are generated in the city by 25%. Gardens can be constructed only in cities next to a river or lake.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Totus mundus agit histrionem"[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Inscription above main entrance to the Globe Theatre[NEWLINE][TAB]

Each source of [ICON_RES_WHEAT] Wheat [ICON_RES_BANANA] Bananas and [ICON_RES_DEER] Deer worked by this City produce +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Allows [ICON_FOOD] Food to be moved from this city along trade routes inside your civilization.
The Granary increases the [ICON_FOOD] Food intake of a city, speeding up the city's growth. It's useful when you want to create a large city, fast.
Can only be built by Alderdice.
The Grandstand can only be built by Alderdice, and replaces the Stadium. Unlike the Stadium, it provides [ICON_CULTURE] Culture, helping to expand territory and gain new Social Policies more quickly.
Unlocks Biltmore House when built in every city.
Provides a boost to [ICON_GOLD] Gold and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. Build one in each city to unlock the Biltmore House national wonder.
Doubles religious pressure emanating from this City.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Must be built in a Holy City. Must have built a Temple in all Cities. The cost goes up the more cities there are in the empire.

An important building for a civilization trying to spread their religion world-wide from an empire with few, populous cities. Must be built in a Holy City. Doubles religious pressure emanating from this city. A civilization must have a Temple in all cities before it can construct the Grand Temple.

A Grand Temple is a revered holy site held sacred among the followers of a given religion. These temples often feature grand architecture and ornate inscriptions that stand for centuries as a testament to the faith of the religion's adherents. Although there is no clear consensus as to which of the many temples found throughout the world today is the oldest, many believe the Göbekli Tepe - found in modern Turkey and assembled over 12,000 years ago - to be the earliest man-made religious structure ever discovered.

99.9% reduction in effectiveness of enemy spies in the city in which it is built. All other cities in the civilization get a 25% reduction in enemy spy effectiveness. Negates the [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism bonus from other players' Internet technology.
The Great Library provides a free technology, plus +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 Great Scientist point. This Wonder can provide a big early-game tech boost at a fairly cheap production cost.

The Great Lighthouse increases the movement and sight of all military naval units by +1. It also provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 Great Merchant point. Obviously, this is an extremely useful for any naval-oriented civilization, especially in a game with a lot of islands or small continents.

The Great Wall increases the movement cost for entering a tile within your territory by +1 for all enemy units. It also provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 Great Engineer point. The defensive benefits of this Wonder, particularly for a sprawling empire with a road network, are incalculable. Enemy assaults will be grindingly slow, allowing you to send reinforcements to the most threatened spots long before the attacks can materialize.
The Gunsmith Shop increases the speed at which the city produces Gunpowder Units.

The Hagia Sophia increases your cities' generation of [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great People by 25%. In addition, it provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 Great Artist point. This Wonder can be enormously powerful in a civilization that's employing a lot of specialists.

The Hanging Gardens increase the population of all of your cities by +1, and it increases your civilization's happiness by +3 for your entire empire. This fairly inexpensive Wonder is helpful to any civilization, but especially to an expansionist civilization with a lot of cities.

Unique German Bank replacement. +5% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production for each Trade Route your civilization has with a City-State. Trade routes other players make to a city with a Hanse will generate an extra 1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the city owner and the trade route owner gains an additional 1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the trade route.

In addition to the regular abilities of the Bank (additional [ICON_GOLD] Gold output, and additional [ICON_GOLD] Gold from Trade Routes), the Hanse provides [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production for each Trade Route within your civilization that connects to a City-State. The Trade Routes can come from any combination of cities, even cities without the Hanse (Example: If you have trade routes from Berlin to Geneva, Munich to Geneva, Munich to Berlin, and Berlin to Brussels, then all cities with the Hanse would get +15% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production). Only Germany may build it.

Forms a [ICON_CONNECTED] City Connection with the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital over water (if they're not already [ICON_CONNECTED] connected by land). Sea trade routes originating from this city have a 50% increase in range and produce an additional 1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold when connecting to another civilization.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must be built on the coast.

A harbor is a sheltered body of water that provides protection from the elements for boats and ships at anchor within. Where there are some "natural" harbors, most have required some degree of dredging, the construction of breakwaters and windbreaks, and the like. In addition, harbors also possess docks and jetties for loading and unloading cargo as well as warehouses to store the goods passing through.

The Harbor is a Medieval-era building. It improves the range and [ICON_GOLD] Gold yield of sea trade routes. It allows "water city connections" (see rules) between cities. The Harbor also increases the [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production output of an improved sea resource.

+50% [ICON_CULTURE] Culture in this City. Contains 3 slots for Great Works of Art.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Must have built an Opera House in all Cities. The cost goes up the more cities there are in the empire.

The Hermitage is a museum in Saint Petersburg, Russia. Constructed in 1764 by Catherine the Great, the Hermitage's collection contains some three million pieces, including the largest collection of paintings in the world. The collection is housed in a number of historic buildings, including the extraordinary Winter Palace, the former official residence of the Tsars from 1732 to 1917.
This National Wonder increases the cultural output of the city in which it is constructed by 50%. It cannot be constructed unless the civilization has an Opera House built in all of its cities.

All newly-trained non-air Units in this City receive the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Morale[ENDCOLOR] Promotion, improving [ICON_STRENGTH] combat strength by 15%. Contains 1 slot for a Great Work of Writing.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Must have built a Barracks in all Cities. The cost goes up the more cities there are in the empire.

From ancient times, a "heroic epic" is a poem that defines a people or an era, and is usually centered upon the heroic actions of one or more people. The "Odyssey" is such a work, as is the Mesopotamian "Epic of Gilgamesh" and the Anglo-Saxon "Beowulf."

This National Wonder gives all units built in this city the "Morale" promotion, increasing their combat strength by +15%. It also provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. The Heroic Epic can be constructed when a civilization has a barracks in all of its cities.

The Himeji Castle Wonder gives a +20% bonus to combat strength to units fighting in friendly territory, as well as +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 Great Engineer points. This Wonder is an awesome addition to your nation's defenses. It doesn't help your cities fight, though, so make sure that you're using military units in your defense!

A hospital is an institution for diagnosing and treating the sick or injured, and for housing them during their recovery. Many hospitals are also teaching institutions, where student doctors and nurses learn their trade. The earliest hospitals were temples to certain gods associated with health and healing. Religious hospitals were established in Sri Lanka by 430 BC, and King Asoka of India created a chain of hospitals across Hindustan around 230 BC.
The Hospital is an Industrial-era building. It's useful when you want to create a large city, fast.

50% of the [ICON_CULTURE] Culture from World Wonders, Natural Wonders, and Improvements (Landmarks, Moai, Chateau) is added to the [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism output of the city. [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism output from Great Works +50%.

With its massive boost to [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism, the Hotel is an excellent choice for civilizations that are trying to achieve a Culture victory, or attempting to increase your ideological impact on other civilizations.
The Hov increases [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness by 1 and [ICON_GOLD] Gold by 2.
+1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production in every tile next to a River. Requires 1 [ICON_RES_ALUMINUM] Aluminum.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must be built next to a River.

The Hydro Plant is a mid-game building which can only be constructed in a city which is adjacent to a river. The Hydro Plant increases the [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production output of every tile the city works which is also adjacent to the river. Constructing the Hydro Plant consumes 1 [ICON_RES_ALUMINUM] Aluminum.
Unique Zulu Barracks replacement. Grants unique promotions to pre-gunpowder melee units.

In addition to the regular abilities of the Barracks which it replaces, the Ikanda grants a unique set of promotions to pre-gunpowder melee units created within the city. These include faster movement, and greater combat strength. Only the Zulu may build it.
Provides an additional spy and levels up all your existing spies. Also provides a 15% reduction in enemy spy effectiveness. Must have a Police Station in all cities.

An important defensive National Wonder for a technology-driven civilization. The National Intelligence Agency provides an additional spy, levels up all your existing spies, and provides a 15% reduction in enemy spy effectiveness. A civilization must have a Police Station in all cities before it can construct the National Intelligence Agency.

A National Intelligence Agency provides government resources for the acquisition of information and intelligence data key to providing security and national defense. Everything from covert operations, including espionage and infiltration, to the assessment of national security risks and response recommendations are made by these agencies. The Central Intelligence Agency of the United States is perhaps the most famous (or notorious) of the world's intelligence agencies, as the program has continually influenced global affairs through various means for decades.

+1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production from Scientists, and +1 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science from Engineers. Great Scientists provide 33% more [ICON_RESEARCH] Science when used to discover new technology. May only be built collaboratively through the World Congress.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Building one space station for everyone was and is insane; we should have built a dozen."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Larry Niven[NEWLINE][TAB]
Must have built a Patent Office in all cities.
The Inventor's Hall may only be built once each of your cities has a Patent Office, and you may only build one in your empire. It provides a boost to [ICON_GOLD] Gold and [ICON_RESEARCH] Science.
Must have built a Workshop in all Cities. The cost goes up the more cities there are in the empire.

An ironworks is a facility where iron ore is purified and fashioned into iron or steel. The process begins with exposing the raw material to extremely high heat, and after possibly mixing in other materials, results in some form of purified iron or steel. Iron smelting dates back at least to 1200 BC, and perhaps earlier. Not surprisingly, ironworks are dangerous places, and they require tough, highly-skilled and courageous workers.
The Ironworks National Wonder increases a city's [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production by 8 [ICON_PRODUCTION]. A civilization must have a workshop in all cities before it can construct an Ironworks.

The Kremlin increases the bonus from defensive buildings in all cities by 25%. It also provides +3 culture, +12 Defense and +1 Great Scientist point. Obviously, this Wonder is most effective if you're constructing the requisite defensive buildings - walls, castles, etc. - but its +4 culture bonus is pretty nifty in itself.
+15 XP for all Units. [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and [ICON_GOLD] Gold costs of acquiring new tiles reduced by 25% in this city.
City must have a Public School.

The Research Laboratory is a late-game building which greatly increases the [ICON_RESEARCH] Science output of a city. The city must already possess a Public School to construct the Research Laboratory.
+1 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science for every 2 [ICON_CITIZEN] Citizens in this City.
The Library increases the [ICON_RESEARCH] Science output of the city, speeding up the civ's acquisition of new technology.

+1 [ICON_FOOD] Food from Coast and Ocean Tiles. +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production from Sea Resources worked by this City.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Each source of [ICON_RES_FISH] Fish worked by this City produces +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must be built on the coast.

The Lighthouse can only be constructed in a city next to a coastal tile. It increases the [ICON_FOOD] Food output of water tiles and [ICON_RES_FISH] Fish and it increases the [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production output of all sea resources.
[ICON_CULTURE] Culture and [ICON_GOLD] Gold costs of acquiring new tiles reduced by 25% in this city.

The Lion's Gate is the Hittite unique building, replacing Walls. The Lion's Gate increases a city's Defense Strength, making the city more difficult to capture. In addition, the Lion's Gate increases the city's cultural border growth by 25% and provides +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
+1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production from each worked Forest tile.

For much of their history, many of the Iroquois people lived in villages containing one or more "Longhouses," communal buildings constructed of wood saplings sheathed in elm bark. In fact, the Iroquois call themselves "Hodenosaunee," which translates into "People of the Longhouse." The longhouses ranged from 40 to 400 feet in length and some 25 feet wide. They were divided into compartments by inner partitions, each connected by an open center aisle. Several compartments would share a cooking fire in the center aisle, with an opening in the roof above acting as a chimney.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Longhouses are efficient structures, cheaper to construct and heat than individual dwellings, thus requiring fewer natural resources than other types of homes. They are representative of the Iroquois' cultural desire to survive and thrive in harmony with the environment around them.
The Longhouse is the Iroquois unique building, replacing the Workshop. It increases the city's [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production output for each forest within the city's radius.

The Louvre provides a free museum in every city in your civilization. It also provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 Great Artist points. Museums aren't cheap and each provides +5 culture points per turn, so this can provide a massive culture boost during the Renaissance.

Can only be built by Curnow.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Provides [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]2 [ICON_RES_URANIUM] Luboric[ENDCOLOR] resources.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Each source of [ICON_RES_URANIUM] Luboric worked by this city provides +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production.

The Luboric Factory can only be built by Curnow. Unlike the Luboric Refinery, which it replaces, the Luboric Factory gives a bonus to [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production which increases with the number of [ICON_RES_URANIUM] Luboric resources worked by the city it is built in. This bonus stacks with Curnow's trait.
Provides [ICON_RES_URANIUM] Luboric resources without needing to own a tile with the resource. With these resources, you can train more landship units for your army.

Machu Picchu provides a 25% [ICON_GOLD] Gold bonus from city connections (road and/or harbor connections between a capital city and other cities). It also provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 Great Merchant points. Requiring the Currency technology, Machu Picchu provides a moderate financial boost in the early mid-game.
+2 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science from Jungle tiles worked by this City.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have a Library.

The Madrasah is a Medieval-era building. It increases the science output of the city, and it's even more effective if the city is near to jungle tiles. The city must already have a Library in order to construct a Madrasah. It also provides [ICON_PEACE] Faith, unlike the University which it replaces.
{1_Num} [ICON_GOLD] Gold per turn spent on Building maintenance in this City.

Markets increase the amount of [ICON_GOLD] Gold a city generates. Trade routes other players make to a city with a Market will generate an extra 1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the city owner and the trade route owner gains an additional 1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the trade route.

The Pyramid is an Ancient-era building unique to the Maya, replacing the Shrine. It increases the [ICON_RESEARCH] Science and [ICON_PEACE] Faith of a city, speeding Research and the civilization's acquisition of Religions.
The Mead Hall increases [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture by 2.
25% of [ICON_FOOD] Food is carried over after a new [ICON_CITIZEN] Citizen is born (effect stacks with Aqueduct).

A medical laboratory is an institution that studies disease and human anatomy using a wide variety of extremely sophisticated and powerful instruments - from ultrasound to cameras the size of an ant to electron microscopes. Most - if not all - of the remarkable advances in medicine in the past 25 years have been made in medical labs. These include the sequencing of human DNA, retro-viruses to battle HIV-AIDS, gene therapy, nano-technology, and more. Much of the increasing cost of healthcare can be attributed to the simple fact that medical laboratories have been remarkably successful at battling illness and prolonging and improving the quality of human life - and these improvements cost huge amounts of money.

The Medical Lab is a late-game building which decreases the amount of [ICON_FOOD] Food a city needs to increase in size by 25%. The city needs to have a Hospital in order to construct the Medical Lab.
+5% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production for each Trade Route your civilization has with a City-State.

The Meeting House provides [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production for each Trade Route within your civilization that connects to a City-State. The Trade Routes can come from any combination of cities, even cities without the Meeting House. Can only be built in cities following a religion with the Meeting Houses belief. Construct this building by purchasing it with [ICON_PEACE] Faith.
+15 XP for all Units.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have an Armory.

The Military Academy is a mid-game building which increases the number of experience points of units constructed in the city. The city must already possess an Armory before the Military Academy can be constructed.
The Military Base is a mid-game building which increases the city's Defensive Strength by 12 and Hit Points by 25. The city must possess an Arsenal before a Military Base may be constructed.
Each source of [ICON_RES_GOLD] Gold and [ICON_RES_SILVER] Silver worked by this City produces +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have at least one of these resources mined nearby.
The Mint can only be constructed in a city with improved gold or silver resources nearby. The Mint increases the [ICON_GOLD] Gold output of each such resource the city has access to.
Each source of [ICON_RES_INCENSE] Incense and [ICON_RES_WINE] Wine worked by this City produce +1 [ICON_PEACE] Faith and +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.

Monasteries increase a city's [ICON_PEACE] Faith and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture output, especially if the city is near to improved Incense and/or Wine resources. Can only be built in cities following a religion with the Monasteries belief. Construct this building by purchasing it with [ICON_PEACE] Faith.

A monument is a structure built to commemorate an important person, event, deity, or concept. The more important monuments are usually constructed near the center of the city, by the ruler's palace, or near the city's main gates. Monuments come in all shapes and sizes, from the Great Sphinx of Giza, Egypt, to the Statue of Liberty in New York City, USA, to Nelson's Column in London, England. The best of them imbue the city's inhabitants with a great feeling of civic and national pride.
The Monument increases the [ICON_CULTURE] Culture of a city, speeding the growth of the city's territory and the civilization's acquisition of Social Policies.
Can only be built in cities following a religion with the Mosques belief. Construct this building by purchasing it with [ICON_PEACE] Faith.

The Mud Pyramid Mosque is a Songhai unique building, replacing the Temple. The Mud Pyramid Mosque greatly increases the city's [ICON_CULTURE] Culture, speeding the growth of the city's territory and the civilization's acquisition of Social Policies. The Mud Pyramid Mosque has no maintenance costs.
Provides +2 [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism after Flight is researched.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have Walls.

The Mughals were an Islamic empire that invaded India in the 15th century, and ruled most of the subcontinent until the mid-19th. During their rule they constructed elaborate forts across the countryside which served as administrative centers and living quarters for the occupiers. These forts were beautiful structures, fitting palaces for the rulers of a vast empire. Several - including the magnificent "Lahore Fort" and Red Fort of Agra - survive today and remain as some of the largest tourist attractions to India, monuments to the Mughals' power and style.

The Mughal Fort is a Medieval-era building that increases the city's Defense Strength by 7, Hit Points by 25, and provides some [ICON_CULTURE] Culture every turn. It is the Indian unique building, replacing the Castle. After Flight is learned, it provides +2 [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism as well. Building Walls is a prerequisite for building the Mughal Fort.

The Museum is a mid-game building which increases the city's [ICON_CULTURE] Culture output. The city must possess an Opera House (or a Ceilidh Hall) in order to construct the Museum. Contains 2 slots for Great Works of Art.

Provides 3 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great Person Points (GPP) towards a Great Musician. Add up to two specialists to this building to gain [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and increase the rate of Great Musician acquisition (3 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and 3 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] GPP per specialist).

The Musicians' Guild is the only building that contains musician specialist slots, which are critical for generating Great Musicians. If your goal is a cultural victory, this building is a must-have. The Musicians' Guild provides 3 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great Person Points, and each assigned specialist provides 3 [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great Person Points and 3 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.
Must have built a Library in all Cities. The cost goes up the more cities there are in the empire.

A national college is a state-run institute of higher learning. The modern college can be traced back to medieval Islamic madrasah, institutes of law and theology usually associated with mosques. Most countries in the world now have public college and university systems. The University of Tokyo in Japan is one such public institution. According to the Russian Global Universities Ranking, the University of Tokyo is the most prestigious university in Asia and third in the world.

The National College National Wonder increases a city's [ICON_RESEARCH] Science output by 50%, and it provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. A civilization must have a library in all cities before it can construct a National College.

+25% [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great People generation in this City. Contains 1 slot for a Great Work of Writing.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Must have built a Monument in all Cities. The cost goes up the more cities there are in the empire.

A national epic is a poem or story which describes the origin of a nation, its character, or a significant event in its existence. The "Epic of Sundiata" is a Malinese national epic. "The Song of Hiawatha" is a United States national epic. The "Kalevala" is an epic of Finland. In a more modern form, "War and Peace" might be considered a Russian national epic, and "Roots: The Saga of an American Family" another American epic.

This National Wonder increases a city's [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great People generation by 25%. It also provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. A civilization must have a monument in all cities before it can construct a National Epic.

Must have built a Market in all Cities. The cost goes up the more cities there are in the empire. Trade routes other players make to a city with an East India Company will generate an extra 4 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the city owner and the trade route owner gains an additional 2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the trade route.

A National Treasury houses a civilization's wealth, gold, priceless items, and jewels, all under secure lock and key. Records show that some of the first treasuries were constructed by the ancient Greeks, who attached these buildings to temples in order to house all manner of gifts to the gods. Now a National Treasury is usually administered by a branch of government, and usually isn't attached to some religious building or other. The treasury branch not only keeps an eye on a civilization's accumulated wealth, but also governs other financial matters for the nation, like the fine tradition of taxation.

This National Wonder increases [ICON_GOLD] Gold output in a single city by 8. It also provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. A civilization must have a Market in all cities before it can construct a National Treasury.
+15% [ICON_FOOD] Food. Each worked Floodplain tile provides +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must be built next to a River.
The Nilometer is the Egyptian unique building, replacing the Watermill. It increases the city's food and gold output, and should be built if the city is near a river.

Notre Dame provides +5 happiness empire-wide, plus +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 Great Merchant point. By mid-game happiness can be a big problem, especially for expansionist civilizations. Notre Dame is one potent answer.
Requires 1 [ICON_RES_URANIUM] Uranium. City must not contain a Solar Plant.

The Nuclear Plant significantly increases a city's productivity. A Nuclear Plant requires one [ICON_RES_URANIUM] Uranium resource to be constructed. The city must possess a Factory before it can be constructed.
City must be built next to a Mountain.
The Observatory can only be constructed in a city next to a mountain tile. The Observatory greatly increases the city's [ICON_RESEARCH] Science output.

The Opera House is a Renaissance-era building which increases a city's [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. The city needs to have an Amphitheater in order to construct the Opera House. Contains 1 slot for a Great Work of Music.

The Oracle provides a free social policy as well as +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 Great Scientist points. This fairly cheap early-era Wonder can provide a big boost to the civilization that builds it. It's also extremely flexible, since you can use it to acquire the social policy that suits your current situation.
1 Free Technology. Contains 2 slots for Great Works of Writing.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Must have built a University in all Cities. The cost goes up the more cities there are in the empire.

Oxford University is the oldest university in England, and in all of the English-speaking world. Founded sometime late in the 11th century, Oxford has been in continuous operation ever since. Famous Oxford graduates include Roger Bacon, William of Ockham, Sir Walter Raleigh, John Donne, Jonathan Swift, Dr. Samuel Johnson, Oscar Wilde, Sir Richard Burton, and J.R.R. Tolkien.
The Oxford University National Wonder provides 1 free technology and +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture. The civilization must have a university in all cities before it can construct Oxford University.
Can only be built in cities following a religion with the Pagodas belief. Construct this building by purchasing it with [ICON_PEACE] Faith.

Indicates this City is the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital of the empire. Contains 1 slot for a Great Work of Art.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][ICON_CONNECTED] Connecting other Cities to the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital by Road will produce additional [ICON_GOLD] Gold.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]+3 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, +3 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science, +3 [ICON_GOLD] Gold

Your palace is the seat of your government. Early in the game it provides a significant portion of your capital city's culture, gold, science, and production. It also forms the heart of your empire's trading system. Although the palace is automatically rebuilt in another city if your capital is captured, it can still be a terrible blow to your civilization (and it makes it impossible for you to win a Domination victory until you get it back). Protect your palace!
+1 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science for every 2 [ICON_CITIZEN] Citizens in this City. +2[ICON_GOLD] Gold.

Paper was invented in China and dates back as far as 200 BC. As best as can be determined, it was originally used as a packing material, with the earliest surviving example of writing on paper dating to perhaps 8 BC. By 300 AD writing paper was in widespread use across China. The Chinese Paper Maker workshops were highly advanced for their day, creating clean, sturdy paper for the Chinese educated classes, merchants, and the Imperial Court centuries before the first sheet reached the Arabic and European world.

The Paper Maker is the Chinese unique building, replacing the Library. The Paper Maker increases the city's acquisition of [ICON_RESEARCH] Science and also provides a boost to the city's intake of [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"Earth proudly wears the Parthenon as the best gem upon her zone."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - Ralph Waldo Emerson[NEWLINE][TAB]
Unlocks Inventor's Hall when built in every city.
Provides a boost to [ICON_GOLD] Gold and [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, as well as a slot for a Scientist specialist.

The Pentagon Wonder places a free military academy in every city and it increases the rate at which Great Generals are generated by 50%. Finally, it provides 1 culture and +1 Great Merchant points. Since a military academy provides a huge XP bonus to units, this is a seriously useful Wonder for any civilization expecting a lot of late-game combat.
Must have built an Automated Factory in all cities.

The Perpetual Motion Engine may only be built once each of your cities has an Automated Factory, and you may only build one in your empire. It provides an enormous boost to [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production as well as a moderate bonus to [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
Unlocks Carnegie Hall when built in every city.
Provides a large boost to [ICON_CULTURE] Culture as well as some [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness. Build one in each city to unlock the Carnegie Hall national wonder.
Reduces enemy spy stealing rate by 25%.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have a Constabulary.
Police stations slow down the rate at which enemy spies can steal technologies from your city. The city must possess an Constabulary in order to construct the Police Station.

The Porcelain Tower provides +2 science from every specialist in every city. It also gives +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 Great Scientist points. Obviously, this is the perfect Medieval-era Wonder for anyone going for technological supremacy. If you're going to build this Wonder, you ought to assign as many specialists in your cities as you reasonably can. For an extra benefit, make them science specialists to get a potent multiplying effect upon your technological growth.

[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"This loss (of freedom) means the fading from human life of values infinitely precious to it. There only remain ironbound conditions of employment and trivial amusements for leisure."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - A.N. Whitehead[NEWLINE][TAB]
+1 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science for every 2 [ICON_CITIZEN] Citizens in this City.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have a University.

The Public School is a mid-game building which greatly increases a city's output of [ICON_RESEARCH] Science. The city must have already constructed a university or wat in order to build a Public School.

The Pyramids provide a free granary in every city. They also give you +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 Great Engineer point. Granaries increase a city's food intake by +2 food per turn. This earliest of Wonders will speed city growth for the entirety of the game, making it one of the most potent Wonders of all.
Provides 2 [ICON_RES_ALUMINUM] Aluminum. Maximum of 5 of these buildings in your empire.
Each Recycling Center provides 2 [ICON_RES_ALUMINUM] Aluminum. Maximum of 5 of these buildings in your empire.
[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB]"When we build, let us think that we build forever."[NEWLINE][TAB][TAB] - John Ruskin[NEWLINE][TAB]

Unique Assyrian Library replacement. +1 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science for every 2 [ICON_CITIZEN] Citizens in this City. Also has a slot for a Great Work of Writing which, when filled, gives extra XP to trained Units.

In addition to the [ICON_RESEARCH] Science output of the Library it replaces, the Royal Library also has a Great Work of Writing slot. Once filled with a Great Work, it provides extra XP to Units trained in this city, so place a Great Work here as soon as possible for the maximum benefit. Only the Assyrians may build it.

City must have a Market. Trade routes other players make to a city with a Satraps Court will generate an extra 1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the city owner and the trade route owner gains an additional 1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the trade route.

A "satrap" is the title of a provisional governor in the Achaemenian Empire of Persia. The satraps were appointed by the king, and were usually members of the royal family. A powerful figure, the satrap collected taxes and was the supreme judicial figure in the province. He was responsible for raising and maintaining an army, and therefore had to be highly trusted by the monarch. As the central power of the Persian empire weakened during the 5th century BC, the Satraps grew more independent, and some were in fact more powerful than the king they allegedly answered to.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Alexander maintained the satrapal administration after he conquered Persia, sometimes replacing the Satraps with his generals and sometimes retaining the existing governors if they maintained the peace and kept paying their taxes.

The Satrap's Court is the Persian unique building. It replaces the Bank. Like a bank the Satrap's Court increases the city's output of wealth. However, the Satrap's Court also increases the civilization's [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness. The city must have a Market before the Satrap's Court may be constructed.

+1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and [ICON_GOLD] Gold from Sea Resources worked by this City. +15% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production when building Naval Units.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must be built on the coast.
A Seaport increases the [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production output of an improved sea resource.
The Shrine is the earliest building that increases the [ICON_PEACE] Faith generated by a city, allowing you to found and spread religions.

The Sistine Chapel Wonder increases the cultural output of ALL cities by 50%, and it provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 Great Artist points as well. This is one of the more powerful Renaissance-era cultural Wonders.
City must be built on or next to Desert and must not contain a Nuclear Plant.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have a Factory.

A Solar Plant is a late-game building which significantly increases a city's [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production. The city must be constructed on or adjacent to a desert tile in order to build the Solar Plant. The city must possess a Factory before it can be constructed.
+50% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production when building Spaceship Parts. Requires 1 [ICON_RES_ALUMINUM] Aluminum.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have a Factory.

The Spaceship Factory increases the speed at which a city constructs spaceship parts. The Spaceship Factory requires one [ICON_RES_ALUMINUM] Aluminum resource, and the city must possess a Factory before it can be constructed.

The Staatsmuseum is a Boer-unique building which increases the city's output of [ICON_CULTURE] Culture (especially when housing Great Works). It comes pre-built with 1 Great Work. A European civs capturing a city with a Staatsmuseum will gain VP for capturing artifact(s). It replaces the Museum.

+15% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production when building Mounted Units.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Each source of [ICON_RES_HORSE] Horses [ICON_RES_SHEEP] Sheep and [ICON_RES_COW] Cattle worked by this City produce +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have at least one of these resources improved with a Pasture.

The Stable can only be constructed in a city near to one or more improved [ICON_RES_HORSE] horse, [ICON_RES_SHEEP] sheep or [ICON_RES_COW] cattle resources. The Stable increases the speed of production of mounted units.
It cannot provide more [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness than there are [ICON_CITIZEN] Citizens in a city. City must have a Zoo.

A Stadium is a Modern-era building which increases the [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness of your empire, but it cannot provide more happiness than there are citizens in the city. The city must already possess a Zoo before it can construct a Stadium.

The Statue of Liberty provides +1 production and +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture from every specialist in every city. In addition it provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 Great Merchant points. This is a deceptively powerful wonder, highly useful to those leaders who carefully manage their cities.

The Stave Church increases the [ICON_PEACE] Faith of a city, speeding up the rate at which you can found and spread religions. The city must contain a Shrine before the Stave Church can be constructed. The Stave Church has no maintenance cost and takes half the time to build as the Temple, which it replaces.

The Stele is an Ancient-era building unique to Ethiopia, replacing the Monument. It increases the [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and [ICON_PEACE] Faith of a city, speeding the growth of the city's territory and the civilization's acquisition of Social Policies and Religions.

This early-game Wonder provides a free monument in every city, as well as +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 Great Engineer point. Since monuments provide culture, this Wonder is a smart way to increase the size of your early cities and speed up the acquisition of social policies as well.

Each source of [ICON_RES_MARBLE] Marble and [ICON_RES_STONE] Stone worked by this City produce +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must have at least one of these resources improved with a Quarry.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]City must not be in Plains.

Stone Works can only be constructed in a city near an improved [ICON_RES_STONE] Stone or [ICON_RES_MARBLE] Marble resource. Stone Works increase a city's [ICON_PRODUCTION] production. The city must not be in Plains.
Must have built a Subterranean Outpost in all cities.

The Subterranean Colony may only be built once each of your cities has a Subterranean Outpost, and you may only build one in your empire. It provides a large boost to [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.
Unlocks Subterranean Colony when built in every city.
Provides a large boost to [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production as well as some [ICON_RESEARCH] Science. Build one in each city to unlock the Subterranean Colony national wonder.

Trade routes other players make to a city with an Suez Canal will generate an extra 4 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the city owner and the trade route owner gains an additional 2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the trade route. Only one allowed in the world.

The Suez Canal increases the amount of [ICON_GOLD] Gold a city generates. Trade routes other players make to a city with an Suez Canal will generate an extra 4 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the city owner and the trade route owner gains an additional 2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold for the trade route. Only one allowed in the world.

The Sydney Opera House is one of the grandest modern opera houses in the world. Constructed over a 20-year period ending in 1973, the Sydney Opera House is a beautiful building sitting atop Bennelong Point alongside Sydney Harbor in Sydney, Australia. Designed as a series of shells, or wings, the structure is one of the most recognizable in the world and it has come to symbolize Australia itself, in much the same way that the Statue of Liberty symbolizes the United States or the Great Pyramids symbolize Egypt. It houses an Opera Theatre, Concert Hall, three smaller venues, and a restaurant.
The Sydney Opera House is a late-game Wonder that assists a player in achieving a Cultural Victory. It can only be built in a coastal city.

The Taj Mahal increases the length of a civilization's Golden Age by 50%. It also adds +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 Great Artist points. If your civilization creates a lot of Golden Ages, this wonder can really boost their effects dramatically.

The Temple increases the [ICON_PEACE] Faith of a city, speeding up the rate at which you can found and spread religions. The city must contain a Shrine (or a Pyramid) before the Temple can be constructed.
Provides a large boost to [ICON_RESEARCH] Science as well as some [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
It cannot provide more [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness than there are [ICON_CITIZEN] Citizens in a city. City must have a Colosseum.

The oldest known zoological menagerie (or "zoo") has been excavated at Hierakonpolis and dates to c. 3500 BC; the oldest existing zoo, the Tiergarten Schoenbrunn in Vienna, evolved from the exotic animal collection maintained by the Habsburg dynasty and was opened to the public in 1765 AD.

A Zoo increases the [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness of your empire, but it cannot provide more happiness than there are citizens in the city. The city must possess a Colosseum before the Zoo can be constructed.
Can only be built by Griggs.

The Torus Dynamo can only be built by Griggs. It provides a boost to a city's [ICON_RESEARCH] Science greater than the Tesla Coil, which it replaces. This bonus can be very helpful for picking up older technologies you may have missed, or when working towards expensive Future Era technologies.

Must have built a Hotel in all Cities. The cost goes up the more cities there are in the empire. 100% of the [ICON_CULTURE] Culture from World Wonders, Natural Wonders, and Improvements (Landmarks, Moai, Chateau) is added to the [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism output of the city. [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism output from Great Works +100%.

With its massive boost to [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism, the National Visitor Center is an excellent choice for civilizations that are trying to achieve a Culture victory, or attempting to increase your ideological impact on other civilizations. Build it in your top [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism city once all your cities have completed Hotels.
Provides a large boost to [ICON_RESEARCH] Science as well as some [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.

The Turkish Bath is the Ottoman unique building. Like a stock exchange the Turkish Bath increases the city's wealth. A "Wat" is a Buddhist monastery temple found in Cambodia, Thailand, or Laos. The literal translation of "wat" is "school", and indeed the Siamese wats were both places of worship and of learning. A wat consists of a temple containing statues of the Buddha, a prayer room, a room containing religious texts, a pavilion for relaxation, a library, study hall, bell towers, and living quarters. It may be a single building or a collection of structures - a town in itself. Constructed in the 12th century, the Angkor Wat in Angkor, Cambodia, is one of the largest and best-preserved wats in Southeast Asia.
